cases.purpose: Lone ESC followed by a 300 ms pause is ESC and the next byte decodes alone; ESC then '[A' 20 ms later (inside the 50 ms grace) is Up; ESC then '[A' 300 ms later is ESC, '[' and 'A' as separate keys; EOF reads none.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 tw.py 1b s300 71 | { for i in 1 2 3; do wgetch read 0; done; } > lone
/usr/bin/python3 tw.py 1b s20 5b41 | { for i in 1 2; do wgetch read 0; done; } > within
/usr/bin/python3 tw.py 1b s300 5b41 | { for i in 1 2 3 4; do wgetch read 0; done; } > after
cases.oracle: wgetch help text: 50 ms ESC grace and total ESC-sequence cap max(400 ms, ESCDELAY*8); read HANDLE|FD prints 'NAME CODE' from its key table (key_up 257, esc 27, char N, none 0 at EOF); BASHESCDELAY sets the grace.
cases.comparison: contract: decoded key lines from a timed pipe writer (20 ms vs 300 ms margins around the 50 ms grace)

cases.purpose: The same grace applies when reading through an opened screen handle (open 0 NAME): split Up within the grace decodes, a late continuation splits.
